messages:
Aisha M.: Quick Q from last week's Euro night-train: I booked sleeper berths on the company card but one colleague paid the couchette upgrade (cash) because they wanted a lower bunk. The conductor gave a tiny paper stub with just amount and code, no merchant name. Can we claim that? Also the train invoice shows VAT but is in my name only.
Maya (People Ops): Short answers: upgrade/couchette = actuals (attach stub). If stub lacks merchant, attach photo + note with train operator and carriage/berth number. VAT reclaim needs invoice in company name/address; ask operator for a reissued invoice. For missing merchant on stub, Finance may accept if you provide corroborating evidence (ticket QR, card line, or photo).
Tom (Finance): If the colleague paid cash and you want to split: best is the original payer submits the full amount and lists attendees in the split field (or the payer submits and others create matching reimbursement items referencing the same receipt). For the stub with no merchant, submit with "lost merchant" note and attach a screenshot of the online booking or the conductor's ticket QR. For amounts > $75 we prefer an original invoice; exceptions reviewed case-by-case.
Luca R.: Is overnight accommodation on sleeper considered lodging for per-diem rules or something else? I.e., can I mix per-diem and actuals across the same travel day?
Maya (People Ops): Sleepers are lodging (actuals). Per-diem covers meals/incidental tips only and you cannot claim per-diem for days where you claim meal receipts. You can mix: e.g., actual lodging + per-diem for meals on the same day, just don't double-claim meals.
ExpenseBot: :receipt: Missing receipt policy reminder: - amount <= $25: Lost-Receipt Form accepted - $25 < amount <= $75: Lost-Receipt Form + manager approval - amount > $75: original receipt required unless Finance approves exception. Required receipt fields: date, amount, currency. Merchant preferred.
Aisha M.: The conductor refused to reissue a proper invoice. I do have the online booking PDF (shows company billing for berths but upgrade is listed as "onboard cash"). Will that be enough to reclaim VAT?
Tom (Finance): If the booking PDF lists company name for the base berths but the onboard upgrade is cash under a different label, "VAT reclaim" for the upgrade is unlikely. Submit the expense as actuals and flag "VAT reclaim"; Finance will triage but set expectation: reclaim probably only for items on an invoice in company name.
Maya (People Ops): For the split workflow: paste into the expense description something like:
```
Expense: Night-train upgrade (couchette)
Original payer: Luca R.
Split: Luca 10.00, Aisha 10.00, Priya 10.00
Currency: EUR
Notes: conductor stub attached; booking PDF shows base fares billed to company; upgrade paid onboard in cash
```
And attach the stub image + booking PDF + any card statement lines.
Luca R.: Got it. One more: tips paid in cash to the conductor (small) 44d claimable?
Maya (People Ops): Tips: include as actuals if on a receipt or within per-diem if you choose per-diem for that day. Small unreceipted tips follow the missing receipt thresholds.
Aisha M.: Thanks all, I'll submit the full upgrade under Luca's name and add splits + attach the booking PDF. Appreciate the quick help! :thumbsup:
